parts.label: (a)
parts.question_text: State what is meant by diffraction of a wave.
parts.question_text_latex: State what is meant by diffraction of a wave.

parts.label: (b)
parts.question_text:
A beam of vertically polarised light of wavelength 540 nm is incident normally on a diffraction
grating, as shown in Fig. 4.1.
The diffraction grating has a line spacing of 5.0 × 10^{-6} m.
The light transmitted by the diffraction grating illuminates a circular screen. The diffraction
grating is at the centre X of the circle.
The central bright fringe is formed at point O on the screen and has intensity I_{0}.
P is a point on the screen where the line XP is at a variable angle θ to the line XO. The
intensity I of light on the screen at P varies with θ.
parts.question_text_latex:
A beam of vertically polarised light of wavelength 540 nm is incident normally on a diffraction
grating, as shown in Fig. 4.1.
The diffraction grating has a line spacing of $5.0 \times 10^{-6}\,\mathrm{m}$.
The light transmitted by the diffraction grating illuminates a circular screen. The diffraction
grating is at the centre X of the circle.
The central bright fringe is formed at point O on the screen and has intensity $I_{0}$.
P is a point on the screen where the line XP is at a variable angle θ to the line XO. The
intensity I of light on the screen at P varies with θ.

parts.label: (b)(i)
parts.question_text: Show that the angle θ at which the first-order bright fringe is formed is 6.2°.

parts.question_text: On Fig. 4.2, sketch the variation of the intensity I with θ for values of θ from –15° to +15°.

parts.label: (c)
parts.question_text:
A polarising filter is placed in the path of the light beam that is incident on the diffraction
grating in Fig. 4.1. The transmission axis of the filter is at 45° to the vertical.
Suggest how the variation of intensity with θ for the light on the screen compares with the
answer in (b)(iii).
